Topological and Health Diagnosis for Street Networks

Source: R/diagnose.R
walk_diagnose_network.Rd

Evaluates the topological connectivity, dangling nodes, potential undershoots, and component fragmentation of a user-supplied street network before building the routing graph. This function does not alter geometries, leaving repair decisions to the user.

Usage

walk_diagnose_network(data, snap_search_radius_m = 10, crs = NULL)

Arguments

data

An sf object containing LINESTRING or MULTILINESTRING street segments.

snap_search_radius_m

Maximum distance in meters to search for potential undershoots (unconnected ends located near another segment). Default is 10.0 meters.

crs

Optional target metric CRS (e.g. EPSG code or proj4string). If provided, data is transformed to this CRS before distance calculations.

Value

A walk_diagnosis S3 object containing:

summary

Tibble with diagnostic statistics (segments, lengths, components, dangles, undershoots).

components

Table of detected connected components and their total lengths.

undershoots

sf point collection of suspicious dangling endpoints within snap_search_radius_m of another street, with column dist_to_nearest_m.

isolated_edges

sf line collection of edges not belonging to the giant component.

data

Original spatial line data.

search_radius_m

The search radius parameter used.

Details

Concept: Undershoots

An undershoot occurs when a digitized street segment terminates just short of intersecting or connecting with an adjacent road, leaving a small metric gap. While legitimate dead ends (cul-de-sacs) naturally exist in pedestrian networks, a dangling endpoint that lies suspiciously close (within snap_search_radius_m) to another street is typically a digitization or vectorization defect.

In walk_diagnose_network(), undershoots are identified in two stages:

  1. All dangling endpoints (nodes with topological degree = 1) are isolated across the network.

  2. The minimum Euclidean distance from each dangling endpoint to all other line geometries (excluding the incident segment itself) is computed. If this distance is less than or equal to snap_search_radius_m, the endpoint is flagged as a potential undershoot.

In pedestrian routing, even a gap of a few centimeters forms an impassable barrier, artificially forcing detours or disconnecting origins from destinations. Potential undershoots can be resolved during network construction via walk_build_network(..., repair = TRUE, snap_tolerance_m = ...).

Concept: Isolated Edges

Isolated edges are street segments that belong to disconnected components (subgraphs or "islands") outside of the primary giant component (the largest contiguous connected network).

In walk_diagnose_network(), connectivity components are detected using a fast disjoint-set (Union-Find) algorithm implemented in Rust:

  1. Endpoints are matched across lines using coordinate coincidence with 1 mm precision.

  2. The giant component is determined as the component with the largest total network length.

  3. Any edge where neither endpoint connects to the giant component is labeled as an isolated edge.

Isolated fragments commonly arise from bounding box or polygon clipping (cutting streets at administrative borders), gated communities, or disjointed municipal data layers. When routing or computing isochrones, any origin or destination snapped to an isolated edge will be mathematically unreachable from the rest of the city (resulting in infinite travel times).

Visual Inspection

Diagnostic results can be inspected visually using plot(diagnosis) or walk_plot_diagnosis(), which renders the giant component in neutral tones, highlights isolated edges in red, and marks potential undershoots with amber points.

See also

walk_plot_diagnosis(), walk_build_network()

Examples

data(streets_cusco)
diag <- walk_diagnose_network(streets_cusco, snap_search_radius_m = 5)
print(diag)
#> 
#> ── Walkability Network Health Diagnosis ────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Total network analyzed: 484 segments (40.0 km)
#> ✔ Total components detected: 125
#> • Giant (main) component: 68.3% of network (27.3 km)
#> ! Detected 124 disconnected components / islands (12.69 km, 31.7% of network).
#> ℹ Identified 81 potential undershoots (dangling ends located <= 5 m from another street).
#> ! Recommendation: You can fix these by running walk_build_network(..., repair =
#>   TRUE, snap_tolerance_m =
#> 5
#> ).
#> 
#> Run `plot(diagnosis)` to inspect isolated segments and undershoots on a map.
